review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Florida-specific habitat and spawning evidence now replaces generic homepage citations; the configured SST band remains provisional.

profile.diet: Barnacles, oysters, crabs, and fiddler crabs
profile.behavior: Uses human teeth to scrape barnacles and oysters off bridge pilings, seawalls, docks, and rock jetties. Spawns in late winter near inlets.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, cool-water preference ideal for sheepshead.
factors.value_notes: A federal species account reports a broad environmental temperature range of about 8-30 °C, but that is tolerance/context, not a preferred adult SST curve. FWC and Florida Museum habitat accounts do not validate the configured 12-28 °C outer band or 16-24 °C ideal. Keep both numeric intervals provisional.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in shallow piling and dock structure zone.
factors.value_notes: FWC and Florida Museum support shallow coastal habitat around oyster bars, seawalls, pilings, jetties, mangroves and tidal creeks; juveniles also use seagrass and mud, while adults move offshore to spawn. These habitat descriptions support shallow coastal use but do not validate the exact 0.5-15 m range or 1-8 m ideal as a universal bottom-depth preference.

value_text.peak: It is peak winter sheepshead spawning season.
value_text.off: Outside peak winter run, but sheepshead are present year-round around pilings.

factors.value_notes: FWC reports nearshore spawning movement in late winter and early spring, typically March-April. Florida Museum reports early-spring spawning and Gulf larvae recorded January-May. This supports a broad seasonal pattern, but not the configured December-April window or January-March peak scores as a South Florida catch-rate curve.

text.day: It is full daylight, when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

text.rising: The tide is rising, bringing in fresh water and bait.
text.falling: The tide is falling, flushing bait out through structure.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
